title: Observed robot effects enter the shared offline contract
scope: Two new independent saved local Auto rigid pickup branches; no combined MATTERIX/Auto world, original GRID runtime, live adapter, liquid, cameras, agent, training or full reference reproduction.

prelift_opposed_contact_intervals.scope: Observed positive normal force on both pads; not no-slip or intersample grasp proof

rejected_evidence_cases.scope: Offline mutation guards and explicitly constructed acknowledgement/contact counterexamples using actual sample structure. These are not additional native experiments.

provenance_guards: Frozen raw SHA and original JSONL line/JSON pointer retained
Every observation actual ctrl matches logged actual driver
Driver input resolves prior actual observation; collector monotonic ordering retained
Native clock domains and episodes remain separate

Contact-force aggregates recalculated from saved native contact forces; arrival errors, speed norms and sampled holds from saved pose/twist; object lift from saved positions and baseline. No independent native force, pose or velocity reconstruction.
Serialization roundtrip preserves every raw payload
Original schemas and source files unchanged

performance.implementation: Streaming saved JSONL; one raw row plus lightweight observed vectors retained

previous_adapter: The initial 128MiB input adapter was not executed against oversized 348.7/299.6MB traces. Its frozen protocol remains preserved; v2 was separately frozen and run once.
interpretation: The local positive pickup has sampled measured arrival and object-height/contact evidence, and the no-close branch stops at its grasp gate. The shared contract can carry these distinct observed effects. It does not create or prove a joint MATTERIX/Auto episode.
limitations: Positive pad contact is not a no-slip grasp theorem
A 500Hz sampled hold is not proof between samples
Loaded contact-fraction and all-sample contact are reported separately
Collector/native clocks have not been cross-calibrated
Future MATTERIX effect admission requires native fluid/object measurements and same-world causal evidence
